content:
iOS 27 is a major update to Apple's "Photos" app, featuring improvements to slideshow playback and Shared Albums, while also introducing a long-awaited feature reminiscent of the traditional "Camera Roll": "Captured by Me".

iOS 27's "Captured by Me" in the Photos app only displays photos and videos you take with the Camera app

Apple's Photos app has continued to expand its features over the years. Beyond storing photos and videos taken on iPhone, it also includes content shared with you by others, "Memories" highlights, screenshots, saved media, and more.

Previously, the Photos app offered a "Camera Roll" feature similar to today's "Recents" album, which included photos you took yourself and images you saved.

However, there has always been a missing feature—one that truly displays only the photos and videos you personally captured. More accurately, it should be called your "Camera Roll".

iOS 27 introduces this long-awaited feature, called "Captured by Me".

iOS 27's "Captured by Me" is an entirely new collection within the Photos app. As the name suggests, it will only contain media you capture with the Camera app.

This means photos and videos taken with your iPhone will be gathered here, but you won't see screenshots, photos sent by friends, or other types of content.

In addition to this dedicated "Captured by Me" collection, you can also use the "Captured by Me" filter within the main Photos library.

Regardless of which method you use, the "Captured by Me" feature fills an important gap in Apple Photos' functionality.

Do you plan to use this new feature in iOS 27's Photos app? Let us know in the comments.
